FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, MPI libraries, and required certificates.
# A newer version of CMake is required, so we add the Kitware APT repository.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    gnupg \
    wget && \
    wget -O - https://apt.kitware.com/keys/kitware-archive-latest.asc | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg && \
    echo 'deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/kitware-archive-keyring.gpg] https://apt.kitware.com/ubuntu/ jammy main' | tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kitware.list >/dev/null && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone, build, and install Kripke with MPI support.
# This single RUN command performs all build steps and cleans up afterwards
# to minimize the size of the final image, as multi-stage builds are disallowed.
# FIX: The source code is cloned from the 'master' branch, as the requested 'main' branch does not exist.
# The build system produces 'kripke.exe', which is correctly copied to /usr/local/bin/kripke.
# Submodules are initialized recursively with '--recursive' to include the required BLT build system.

    cd /opt/kripke_src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      .. && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke_src

# you will likely need to pass specific arguments to mpirun.
# Example: mpirun -np 4 --allow-run-as-root kripke --groups 16 --zones 512
# The '--allow-run-as-root' flag is often necessary when running as the root user.
# Additional flags for network interface selection may be needed depending on the K8s CNI.

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke benchmark
# within the Flux Framework on a single Kubernetes node.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # Deploys to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to deploy, set to 1 to run on a single node
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI ranks (tasks) to run for the job
  tasks: 4

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux operator
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the CRD
    strict: true

  # Ensure the job resources are not cleaned up after completion for inspection
  cleanup: false

  # The main container specification for the application
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by flux. The Flux Operator prepends 'flux run -n <tasks>'
      command: kripke
      # The main application container is not the launcher pod
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest runs the Kripke benchmark on a specific
# high-performance ARM-based AWS instance, resolving the previous MPI rank error.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-minicluster
  # Deploys to the default namespace as requested
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job will run on one node, as required.
  size: 1
  # Increased tasks to 64 to fully utilize the vCPUs of the selected hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines pod-specific settings, including scheduling constraints.
  pod:
    # Selects a specific AWS instance type for this job, targeting a 64-core ARM machine.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration required for the targeted architecture.
  flux:
    # Specifies the target architecture is ARM.
    arch: "arm"
    # Overrides the default Flux view container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Ensures the job resources are not cleaned up after completion for inspection.
  cleanup: false
